tags.name: Audit logs
tags.description: Audit logs are used to track end-user activities in Logto sign-in experience and other flows. It does not include activities in Logto Console.

get.description:
Get logs that match the given query with pagination.

### Page mode

The default page-based mode uses `page` / `page_size`, returns `Total-Number` and `Link` headers, and includes audit logs only. For tenants with very large log volumes, the default exact `count(*)` may exceed Postgres `statement_timeout`. Pass `enableCap=true` to short-circuit the count query: any tenant with more than 10,000 matching logs saturates `Total-Number` at the sentinel value `10001` and the response includes `Total-Number-Is-Capped: true`. In capped responses the `Link` header omits `rel="last"` and `rel="next"`; walk forward by incrementing `page` and stop on an empty response.

### Cursor mode

Pass `pagination=cursor` to opt into cursor-based reading. Cursor mode returns the same `LogResponse[]` body and reads audit logs only. `end_time` is required and must not be in the future; `start_time` is optional. The page size is controlled by `limit`, which defaults to `500` and is capped at `1000`, and the next page cursor is returned in the `Next-Cursor` response header. Omit `cursor` from the first request to start at the beginning; pass the `Next-Cursor` header value back as `cursor` to continue. The header is omitted on the last or empty page. Keep `start_time`, `end_time`, and the cursor unchanged while paging.

Cursor mode does not run the page-mode count query and does not emit `Total-Number` or `Link` headers. It rejects `page`, `page_size`, `enableCap`, `userId`, `applicationId`, and `logKey` with `400`. The pages are not a consistent snapshot and do not make deleting the same time window lossless: a row whose transaction commits after the cursor has passed its position is absent from the result but would still be removed by a later time-window `DELETE /api/logs`.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Page mode only; rejected in cursor pagination mode. Filter logs by user ID.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Page mode only; rejected in cursor pagination mode. Filter logs by application ID.

parameters.name: logKey
parameters.description: Page mode only; rejected in cursor pagination mode. Filter logs by log key.

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on `createdAt`, in unix milliseconds. When set, returns only logs where `createdAt >= start_time`. Applies to both page and cursor modes. Because the bound is inclusive, when resuming pagination from the last fetched log, pass its `createdAt + 1` as `start_time` (or de-duplicate by log `id`) to avoid re-fetching the boundary log.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on `createdAt`, in unix milliseconds. When set, returns only logs where `createdAt <= end_time`. In cursor mode this parameter is required and values in the future are rejected with `400`. In page mode it remains optional.

parameters.name: enableCap
parameters.description: Page mode only. When `true`, short-circuits the underlying `count(*)` query: any tenant with more than 10,000 matching logs saturates `Total-Number` at the sentinel value `10001` and the response emits `Total-Number-Is-Capped: true`. The `Link` header then omits `rel="last"` and `rel="next"` because the real total is unknown. Default `false`; rejected in cursor mode.

parameters.name: pagination
parameters.description: Set to `cursor` to opt into cursor mode. Omit this parameter for the default page mode. Other values return `400`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `Next-Cursor` header. Pass it back unchanged with the same `start_time` and `end_time`. Only valid with `pagination=cursor`; empty, malformed, or too-long values return `400`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Cursor mode only. Maximum number of logs returned by this page. Default `500`; maximum `1000`. Rejected in page mode and when outside that range.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page mode only. Page number, starting from 1. Rejected in cursor pagination mode.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Page mode only. Number of logs per page. Default `20`; maximum `100`. Rejected in cursor pagination mode.

400.description: Returned when `start_time` or `end_time` is not a finite number, when `start_time > end_time`, or when a page-mode or cursor-mode parameter is invalid or incompatible. Cursor mode requires `end_time`, rejects a future `end_time`, rejects `page`, `page_size`, `enableCap`, `userId`, `applicationId`, and `logKey`, and rejects `cursor` or `limit` without `pagination=cursor`.

200.description: An array of logs that match the given query. In page mode, `Total-Number` and `Link` describe the page-based result set. In cursor mode, a non-empty page includes a `Next-Cursor` header when more rows were found; the header is omitted on the last or empty page.

Total-Number.description: When `enableCap=false`: exact match count. When `enableCap=true`: either the exact count (≤ 10,000) or the saturation sentinel `10001`; inspect `Total-Number-Is-Capped` to distinguish.

Total-Number-Is-Capped.description: Present and set to `true` only when `enableCap=true` and the result has more than 10,000 matching logs (in which case `Total-Number` is `10001`). Consumers should treat `Total-Number` as `> 10,000` when this header is present.

Link.description: Pagination links per RFC 5988. `rel="first"` and `rel="prev"` are emitted as usual. When the response is capped (`Total-Number-Is-Capped: true`), `rel="last"` and `rel="next"` are omitted because the saturated count makes the derived page count unreliable — clients should walk forward by incrementing `page` and stop on an empty response.

Next-Cursor.description: Cursor mode only. Opaque cursor for the next page, present only when more rows were found. Pass it as the `cursor` query parameter with the same time window. It is omitted on the last page and for an empty result.

attempts.description: The number of delivery attempts made for this webhook event.

nextAttemptAt.description: The scheduled time of the next retry attempt, in unix milliseconds. Present only while a retry is pending.

redeliveredFrom.description: The ID of the failed webhook log entry that this manual redelivery was triggered from.

delete.description:
Delete log rows in bounded batches.

`start_time` / `end_time` carry the same inclusive semantics as `GET /api/logs`: a row is deleted when its `createdAt` falls in `[start_time, end_time]`, at millisecond granularity. Note that this operation removes **every** log row in that window, while `GET /api/logs` returns audit logs only. Rows whose transactions commit after a read passes their position are also removed, so purge a window by time only after its data has stopped changing.

Webhook delivery logs (`TriggerHook.*`) share the `logs` table but are not returned by `GET /api/logs`; `DELETE /api/logs` still removes them. `deletedCount` can therefore exceed the number of audit log rows a complete read returned. A window covering the last 24 hours also removes the deliveries counted by the execution stats on `GET /api/hooks`.

`end_time` is required, so a bare `DELETE /api/logs` never means "delete everything". `end_time` must not be in the future and is rejected with `400` otherwise; a common cause is passing microseconds or nanoseconds instead of milliseconds, or a miscomputed timezone offset. Passing seconds instead yields a boundary in the past, which deletes nothing rather than deleting too much.

This operation is irreversible and reachable by any Management API token. Each call deletes at most `limit` rows in a single statement and reports `hasMore`. Keep both bounds fixed across calls and repeat while `hasMore` is `true`; recomputing a boundary between calls would skip rows. Run one cleanup at a time: a concurrent purge can make `hasMore` under-report.

### Performance

`DELETE` marks rows dead and leaves index cleanup to autovacuum, so writes are dominated by heap tuples and WAL. The statement is matched on `ctid`, so the outer side is a Tid Scan over exactly `limit` rows and the inner select reads those row ids from `logs__created_at_id`; expect the cost of a call to track `limit` rather than the size of the table. Measure with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on your own data before running a large purge.

Freed space is reused by later inserts but the table file does not shrink, so disk usage will not drop immediately after a purge.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on `createdAt`, in unix milliseconds, with the same semantics as `GET /api/logs`. Only log rows with `createdAt <= end_time` are deleted. Returns `400` if the value is in the future.

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on `createdAt`, in unix milliseconds, with the same semantics as `GET /api/logs`. Only log rows with `createdAt >= start_time` are deleted. Omit to purge everything up to `end_time`. Returns `400` if it is after `end_time`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows deleted by this call. Default `1000`, maximum `10000`. Returns `400` for values outside that range.

200.description: Summary of the rows deleted by this call. `deletedCount` is the number of log rows deleted, and `deletedRange` is an optional `{ oldest, newest }` object holding the unix-millisecond timestamps of the deleted rows; it is omitted when nothing was deleted. `hasMore` is `true` when `deletedCount` equals `limit`, meaning this batch was full rather than that more rows definitely exist, so the caller should repeat the request with the same bounds.

400.description: Returned when `end_time` is missing, empty, negative, outside the safe integer range, in the future, or not a finite number; when `start_time` is malformed or after `end_time`; or when `limit` is outside `1..10000`.

attempts.description: The number of delivery attempts made for this webhook event.

nextAttemptAt.description: The scheduled time of the next retry attempt, in unix milliseconds. Present only while a retry is pending.

redeliveredFrom.description: The ID of the failed webhook log entry that this manual redelivery was triggered from.
